result.scientific_strategy:
## d1897119-e054-4e2a-a2fd-06958f8ce0bd / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm reach-and-hold distribution. The fresh PPO baseline reached 51.0% on the task-reference panel. Expanding training support to the official radius range raised the transferred checkpoint to 82.5%; unchanged continuation reached 83.0% on the repeated task-reference panel and 87.5% on a fresh 400-episode research panel. The experiment-4 three-band sampler, also transferred, produced the strongest measured policy at 92.5% on task-reference-v1 and 93.5% on the fresh research panel. The campaign has therefore made substantial measured progress, but remains below 98% and has no official confirmation. The sampler improvement is not yet separated from transfer history or learning-process variation.

**Lessons and limits:** The original 14–20 cm training distribution missed the short-radius portion of the official task. Full-radius training recovered short and mid radii but traded away long-radius successes during later optimization; the experiment-3 endpoint was 42/57, 50/59, and 74/84 by radius versus 50/57, 54/59, and 61/84 for its parent. Experiment 4 improved those bands to 52/57, 58/59, and 75/84, with 37 fresh-panel successes unique to the endpoint versus 13 unique to the prior working policy. Its 65536-step proxy/reward peak instead reached 82/84 long-radius successes while scoring lower overall, so training metrics do not reliably select task policies. The repeated task-reference measurements use one fixed panel and the fresh research measurements one seed; all retained training artifacts record seed 0. The sampler changes training exposure only: the protected evaluator, task mechanics, observation layout, action mapping, and policy I/O remain unchanged.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the experiment-4 gain persists from an independent fresh initialization and across new episode panels, rather than reflecting seed, transfer-path, or panel variation. It is also unresolved whether the short- and mid-radius recovery can coexist with the stronger long-radius behavior seen at other checkpoints, and how much of the progression is attributable to radius coverage, targeted exposure, transfer, or later optimization.
